newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan government orders end of CANTV strike.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan government orders end of CANTV strike.

text.p: The Venezuelan government stepped in Wednesday to solve a prolonged strike over wages affecting telephone company CANTV and ordered a legal end to the stoppage, union leaders said.
They said the measure, using the government's constitutional right to intervene in public services, was adopted at the weekly Cabinet meeting.
The latest round of negotiations on Tuesday between union representatives and management had failed to break an impasse over wage contracts.
"The government decreed a return to work and an official arbitration," Audio Rincon, secretary general of the umbrella telecommunications union group Fetratel, told Reuters.
He said the goverment's decision to step in and try and solve the dispute directly was announced by Labor Minister Maria Bernardoni.

Fetratel represents 29 unions which had been on strike since March 13. It said the stoppage involved one third of CANTV's 16,600 workers, a figure disputed by CANTV which said the walkout had not affected operations.
CANTV executive vice-president for human resources Marina de Ratmiroff told reporters Wednesday that "98 percent of the employees are working normally."

She repeated that CANTV was offering a 111 percent pay rise. Union leaders noted this would be phased over up to three years and maintained their demands for an immediate 60 percent wage increase followed by another 40 percent in 1998, plus a number of bonuses and special premiums.
According to Venezuelan legislation, the government is empowered to order the end of a strike "when the paralysis of an essential public service can cause irreparable damage to the public community."
